name: Agent-to-Agent Protocols (A2A)
question: How does my agent hand work to another agent?
summary: A2A lets one agent delegate a task to an opaque remote agent, usually one run by another organisation. The client discovers the remote agent through its Agent Card, sends messages, and tracks a Task through states such as working, input required and completed, by polling, streaming or push notifications, then collects the artifacts it returns. MCP connects an agent to tools; A2A connects agents as peers.
useCases: Handing a whole goal to a partner’s agent: rebooking, claims, estimates
Long-running work with questions back to the requester
Agents built on different frameworks or by different companies

steps.title: Tool or agent?
steps.text: A status lookup is one function: offer a tool or an API. Negotiating an estimate needs judgment, questions back and time, so it is delegated to an agent.

steps.title: Publish your Agent Card
steps.text: The card names the agent, where to reach it, what it can do (streaming, push), its skills and security schemes. Version 1.0 lets you sign it.

steps.title: Discover and verify the remote card
steps.text: Fetch the garage agent’s card from its well-known path, check the signature against keys you trust, and confirm the skill you need is listed.

steps.title: Send a message, get a Task
steps.text: SendMessage starts the work and returns a Task with an id and a state, usually TASK_STATE_WORKING. The remote agent stays opaque: you see states and results, not its tools.

steps.title: Follow states; answer questions
steps.text: Streaming delivers each state change as it happens. INPUT_REQUIRED is an interrupted state: answer it in a new message on the same task and work resumes.

steps.title: Collect artifacts; map failures
steps.text: COMPLETED carries the artifacts, here the approved estimate. FAILED, CANCELED or REJECTED are terminal: hand them to your own retry or escalation policy.

pros: Delegates whole goals across frameworks and organisations
Long-running tasks with questions back, streaming and push
Agent Cards make discovery and security explicit
Remote agents stay opaque: no need to expose their tools
cons: Heavier than a tool call: cards, auth, task state handling
Less predictable than a deterministic API
Trust and signing must be managed across organisations
Fewer production deployments than MCP so far
avoidWhen: A deterministic lookup or action: expose an API or MCP tool
Agents you own in one process: coordinate them with a graph

practice.scenario: An insurer’s claims agent needs a repair estimate agreed for a damaged car. Rather than calling a single garage API, it delegates the whole negotiation to the garage chain’s own agent over A2A: it reads the garage’s Agent Card, sends a task, answers one question (“Approve OEM parts or aftermarket?”) when the task pauses in INPUT_REQUIRED, and receives the approved estimate as an artifact.

industries.use: Claims agents delegating estimates and surveys to partner agents
An agency’s agent handing rebooking to an airline’s own agent
A shipper’s agent asking a carrier’s agent to arrange a pickup and report back

practice.analogy: Hiring a contractor rather than buying a tool. You describe the job, answer their questions as they come up, and receive the finished work, without seeing how they did it.

library.name: A2A Python SDK (a2a-sdk)
library.what: Client and server libraries for the A2A protocol. The example shows the underlying JSON-RPC calls so every field is visible.

practice.note: Raw JSON-RPC against A2A v1.0. verify_card_signature, token and ask_claims_handler stand for your own code; check field names against the specification.

samples.code:
import time, uuid, httpx

BASE = "https://agents.example-garage.in"
card = httpx.get(f"{BASE}/.well-known/agent-card.json").json()
verify_card_signature(card)                           # reject unsigned or unverifiable cards
assert any(s["id"] == "negotiate_estimate" for s in card["skills"])
A2A_URL = f"{BASE}/a2a"                               # the JSON-RPC endpoint the card lists

def rpc(method: str, params: dict) -> dict:
    r = httpx.post(A2A_URL, timeout=30, headers={"A2A-Version": "1.0", "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"},
                   json={"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": str(uuid.uuid4()), "method": method, "params": params})
    r.raise_for_status()
    body = r.json()
    if "error" in body:
        raise RuntimeError(body["error"])
    return body["result"]

def msg(text: str, **ids) -> dict:
    return {"message": {"messageId": str(uuid.uuid4()), "role": "ROLE_USER", "parts": [{"text": text}], **ids}}

res = rpc("SendMessage", msg("Agree a repair estimate for claim CLM-88412 within ₹62,000."))
task = res.get("task", res)
DONE = {"TASK_STATE_COMPLETED", "TASK_STATE_FAILED", "TASK_STATE_CANCELED", "TASK_STATE_REJECTED"}
while task["status"]["state"] not in DONE:
    if task["status"]["state"] == "TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED":   # interrupted, not failed
        question = task["status"]["message"]["parts"][0]["text"]
        res = rpc("SendMessage", msg(ask_claims_handler(question),
                                     taskId=task["id"], contextId=task["contextId"]))
        task = res.get("task", res)
    else:
        time.sleep(5)
        task = rpc("GetTask", {"id": task["id"]})
estimate = task.get("artifacts", [])

numericDrill.question: A remote agent’s task takes 42 s. Your client polls GetTask every 5 s, starting 5 s after sending the message, until it sees the final state. How many GetTask calls does it make? (With streaming it would make none.)
numericDrill.answer: Polls at 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 and 40 s still see WORKING; the poll at 45 s sees COMPLETED. That is 9 GetTask calls, and the result arrives up to 3 s late. Streaming or push notifications deliver it when it happens.

interview.question: When would you use A2A rather than MCP?
interview.answer: MCP connects an agent to tools and data it controls: deterministic functions with schemas. A2A is for delegating a goal to another agent, often another organisation’s, that plans for itself, may ask questions, runs for a long time and returns artifacts. If the job is one stateless function, such as a status lookup, offer an API or MCP tool instead.

interview.question: How does an A2A client handle a long task that needs input?
interview.answer: It sends a message and gets a Task. It follows state changes by polling GetTask, streaming, or push notifications. If the state becomes INPUT_REQUIRED, it reads the question, gets the answer, and sends a new message with the same taskId and contextId; the task returns to WORKING. It stops on a terminal state and collects artifacts.

mistakes.mistake: Treating INPUT_REQUIRED as terminal and marking the task failed
mistakes.fix: Answer the question in a new message on the same task

mistakes.mistake: Accepting any Agent Card fetched over the network
mistakes.fix: Verify the card’s signature and domain before sending data

quiz.question: An insurer’s claims agent wants a garage chain’s own agent to negotiate a repair estimate. Which protocol fits?
options: MCP tools/call on a garage API
A2A: delegate a task to the remote agent
quiz.explanation: Delegating a goal to another organisation’s agent is what A2A is for.

quiz.question: Where does an A2A client look for a remote agent’s card by convention?
quiz.explanation: Agent Cards are published at /.well-known/agent-card.json.

quiz.question: A task’s state becomes INPUT_REQUIRED. What does it mean?
options: The task is interrupted and waiting for input from the client
quiz.explanation: INPUT_REQUIRED is an interrupted state; answer it and work resumes.

quiz.question: Which are terminal task states in A2A? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED and REJECTED are terminal; INPUT_REQUIRED and AUTH_REQUIRED are interrupted.

quiz.question: A partner bank wants only a refund status by UTR number. What should you offer?
options: An A2A agent with an Agent Card
An authenticated API or a read-only MCP tool
quiz.explanation: A deterministic lookup is a function, not a task to delegate.

quiz.question: A remote task takes 42 s and the client polls GetTask every 5 s, starting 5 s after sending. How many polls until it sees the final state?
quiz.explanation: Polls at 5–40 s see WORKING; the 45 s poll sees COMPLETED: 9 polls.

quiz.question: How does A2A describe its relationship to MCP?
options: MCP is vertical (agent to tools); A2A is horizontal (agent to agent)
MCP is for agents, A2A for tools
quiz.explanation: A2A presents MCP as vertical and itself as horizontal; they complement each other.

quiz.question: What does an Agent Card include? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: Cards describe identity, skills, capabilities and security; internals stay opaque.

quiz.question: A client receives a Task in INPUT_REQUIRED. How does it answer?
options: Send a new message with the same taskId and contextId
Wait for the task to time out
quiz.explanation: The answer goes on the same task, which then returns to WORKING.

quiz.question: Which A2A version added signed Agent Cards?
quiz.explanation: v1.0.0, released in March 2026, adds signed Agent Cards.

quiz.question: Why verify an Agent Card’s signature before sending claim data?
options: It proves the card was published by a key you trust, not an impostor
quiz.explanation: Signature checks guard against spoofed cards.

quiz.question: Which delivery modes can a client use to follow a long task? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: A2A supports polling, streaming and push; the remote agent’s internals are opaque.

quiz.question: When did Google announce A2A?
quiz.explanation: Google announced A2A on 9 April 2025; it moved to the Linux Foundation on 23 June 2025.

quiz.question: Which bindings does the A2A specification define? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: The bindings are JSON-RPC 2.0, gRPC and HTTP+JSON/REST.

quiz.question: A client treats INPUT_REQUIRED as terminal and marks tasks failed. What is the effect?
options: Healthy tasks that need one answer are abandoned
quiz.explanation: The task was waiting for input, not failing.

quiz.question: A streamed task completes after 14 s. Polling every 5 s instead, when would the client see completion at the earliest?
quiz.explanation: Polls at 5, 10 and 15 s; the 15 s poll is the first after 14 s.

quiz.question: When is A2A a better fit than a tool call? Select all that apply.
options: The work is long-running and may ask questions back
The remote side is another organisation’s agent that plans for itself
The job is one stateless lookup
You need the lowest possible latency for a single read
quiz.explanation: Delegation suits goals that need judgment and time; single lookups belong in tools or APIs.

quiz.question: What does a completed A2A task return its outputs as?
quiz.explanation: Outputs such as documents or estimates come back as artifacts.

quiz.question: When did A2A join the Agentic AI Foundation?
quiz.explanation: A2A joined the Agentic AI Foundation as a Growth Stage project on 27 August 2026.

quiz.question: Which tools help you build or test A2A agents? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: The SDK and ADK build agents; A2A Inspector validates cards and test tasks.
